projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The sustained connection of 22–23 mobile devices on a weekday night, paired with zero camera motion and no household activity, strongly indicates an unannounced gathering is underway. Steve should verify the situation to ensure safety and manage the unexpected guests.

The sustained presence of 20–25 mobile devices combined with zero camera motion on a weekday evening strongly indicates an unannounced large gathering, likely concentrated in camera blind spots or low-light areas, which may impact security and household routines.

The sustained presence of 20–22 mobile devices alongside zero camera motion on a weekday evening strongly indicates a large gathering concentrated in camera-blind zones (likely outdoors or a closed room) rather than normal household activity. This matters because it suggests guests may be in unmonitored areas, warranting a quick check of outdoor cameras or a status update from Steve.

The sustained presence of 20–23 devices alongside zero camera motion strongly suggests a large group is gathered in a camera-blind zone (like the backyard or garage) or the network is miscounting IoT devices as mobile. This warrants a quick verification to rule out unauthorized guests or a network tracking glitch.

The sustained high device count (20–24) combined with zero camera motion or expected activity from the children and dogs strongly indicates a network presence detection anomaly or stationary IoT devices being miscounted, rather than actual occupancy. This matters because it could mask real security events or trigger unnecessary automations.

The sustained count of 21-24 devices alongside zero camera motion on a weekday afternoon strongly suggests either a false presence detection (counting stationary IoT devices as people) or that the household is actually empty, which could trigger automation conflicts or mask real activity if unverified.

The sustained high device count alongside zero camera motion during a weekday afternoon suggests the presence system is likely registering idle network devices rather than active users, or occupants are confined to camera-blind zones; a quick check is recommended to confirm occupancy status and verify camera functionality.

The sustained 16-20 connected devices combined with zero camera motion (including no dog activity) on a weekday afternoon indicates a likely camera blind spot, network reporting anomaly, or that the house is empty with devices left on Wi-Fi; verify camera feeds and check if the family has left for the afternoon.

The sustained presence of 17-21 connected devices alongside zero camera motion during a weekday afternoon strongly suggests unregistered guests or a network counting anomaly, as the high device count contradicts the expected activity levels for a family of six.

The sustained count of 16-18 'mobile' devices combined with zero camera motion during a weekday morning strongly suggests IoT devices (tablets, smart displays, or laptops) are being misclassified as phones, or multiple guests are present; this matters because it may skew occupancy-based automations or mask true home status.
